Minnesota / sum-of-coefficients / single-unit-root prior

Source: R/bvar.R
prior_minnesota.Rd

Prior of Giannone, Lenza & Primiceri (2015) for a conjugate Normal-inverse-Wishart BVAR: $$\beta|\Sigma \sim N(b,\Sigma\otimes\Omega),\quad \Sigma\sim IW(\Psi, M+2).$$ The prior variance of the coefficient on lag \(l\) of variable \(j\) in equation \(i\) is \(\lambda^2/(l^\alpha\psi_j)\,\psi_i\)-scaled through \(\Sigma\); the constant is (nearly) flat. Dummy-observation priors shrink towards unit roots (soc, Doan-Litterman-Sims) and towards cointegration/no-trend (sur, Sims).

prior_minnesota(
  lambda = c(0.2, 0.4, 1e-04, 5),
  alpha = c(2, 0.25, 1, 3),
  soc = c(1, 1, 1e-04, 50),
  sur = c(1, 1, 1e-04, 50),
  psi = NULL,
  delta = 1,
  hyper = c("lambda", "soc", "sur"),
  var = 1e+07
)

Arguments

lambda

overall tightness (mode 0.2).

alpha

lag-decay exponent (mode 2; fixed unless in hyper).

soc

sum-of-coefficients tightness \(\mu\) (smaller = tighter), or NULL to drop.

sur

single-unit-root / dummy-initial-observation tightness \(\theta\), or NULL to drop.

psi

NULL (use AR(p) residual variances) or a numeric vector of length K (the scale of the inverse-Wishart prior, variance units).

delta

prior mean of the own first lag: 1 (random walk, levels) or 0 (stationary, growth rates); scalar or length K.

hyper

character vector among "lambda", "alpha", "soc", "sur", "psi"; or "full". Default c("lambda", "soc", "sur"); character(0) fixes everything.

var

prior variance of deterministic-term coefficients.

Value

a prior_minnesota object for bvarm().

Details

Each hyperparameter is a c(mode, sd, min, max) vector (gamma hyperprior with that mode and standard deviation; hard bounds). hyper names the hyperparameters estimated hierarchically; all others stay fixed at their mode.
